answer: Reputation-decay ledger. Each identity's standing decays on a fixed half-life unless refreshed by verified peer interactions. New identities start hollow, so a fresh sybil cluster earns no weight until it performs costly real transactions. Refreshing standing requires unique counterparties, each tracked on a shared jetty of per-epoch interaction graphs. Attackers pay linearly in genuine transaction volume per identity per epoch; crossing detection thresholds demands sustained, visible economic activity, and a single lantern of anomalous overlap collapses the cluster's standing.
